note: Early cohort expansion studies by Watts et al. (2024) and Roos et al. (2023) show clinical heterogeneity in FILIP1-related neuromuscular disorder, making variable penetrance of generalized limb muscle weakness plausible.

evidence.text: Roos et al. describe five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families harboring homozygous FILIP1 variants displaying neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness and pathology, and dysmorphic features.

source.title: Bi-allelic variants of FILIP1 cause congenital myopathy, dysmorphism and neurological defects
source.quote: Here, we report on five patients from four unrelated consanguineous families with homozygous FILIP1 variants (two nonsense and two missense)... Patients exhibit a broad spectrum of neurological symptoms including brain malformations, neurodevelopmental delay, muscle weakness and pathology and dysmorphic features.

evidence.text: Watts et al. evaluated additional individuals with FILIP1-associated neuromuscular disease identified through the 100,000 Genomes Project and uniparental disomy, expanding the spectrum of weakness and neuromuscular features.

source.title: FILIP1-associated neuromuscular disorder and phenotypic blending due to paternal UPD6
